title: Baked Ziti
description: A classic layered pasta bake with ground beef, mozzarella, and a rich marinara sauce.
author: Brandon
instructions: Dice the onion and butter a 9x13 inch baking dish.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C).
In a large skillet, brown the diced onion and ground beef over medium heat.
Add spaghetti sauce and simmer 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil.
Add ziti pasta and cook until al dente, about 8 minutes. Drain.
Layer as follows: ½ of the ziti, ½ mozzarella cheese, sour cream, ½ sauce mixture, remaining ziti, ½ mozzarella cheese, remaining sauce mixture.
Top with Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the cheeses are melted.
tips: For a larger meal, use 2 lbs of pasta, but this will require an additional 7x9 inch baking dish.
Use other cheeses, such as Provolone, in addition to Mozzarella and Parmesan.
Serve with extra Parmesan cheese and a shredder.

title: Christmas Crack
description: An addictive holiday treat made with saltine crackers, homemade toffee, and melted chocolate.
author: Brandon
instructions: Line the cookie sheet with nonstick aluminum foil or use regular foil and spray generously with nonstick cooking spray. Prepare toppings such as chopped nuts or sprinkles.
Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Cover the cookie sheet with one layer of saltine crackers.
In a medium saucepan over medium high heat, bring butter and brown sugar to a boil, stirring continuously for about two minutes (it should be bubbly).
Remove from heat, stir in one teaspoon pure vanilla extract.
Pour toffee mixture over crackers, then bake for 6 minutes.
Remove from the oven, sprinkle tops of warm crackers with milk chocolate chips.
Allow chocolate to soften for a minute or two, then spread chocolate evenly on top of crackers.
Add sprinkles or chopped nuts to the top.
Allow to cool, then break up into bite size pieces.
tips: You can speed the cooling process by popping the tray into the freezer.
You can also use white chocolate chips instead of milk chocolate chips.

title: Classic Banana Bread
description: Rich and moist homemade banana bread baked to golden-brown perfection with sweet ripe bananas and cinnamon.
author: Brandon Family
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease an 8x4 inch loaf pan.
In a mixing bowl, mash the ripe bananas with a fork until completely smooth.
Stir the melted butter into the mashed bananas.
Mix in the sugar, beaten egg, and vanilla extract.
Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the mixture and stir in.
Add the flour last, mixing just until incorporated. Do not overmix.
Pour the batter into your prepared loaf pan.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool on a wire rack for 15 minutes before slicing.
tips: The riper and more speckled the bananas, the more naturally sweet and flavorful the loaf.
Optional: fold in ½ cup of chopped toasted walnuts or dark chocolate chips.

title: Honey Beer Bread
description: Hearty, crusty homemade beer bread requiring zero yeast proofing—tender on the inside with a golden buttery crust.
author: Brandon Family
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Grease a standard 9x5 inch loaf pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
Stir in the honey and slowly pour in the beer. Stir gently until just combined (batter will be thick and sticky).
Spread the batter evenly into the prepared loaf pan.
Pour the melted butter evenly over the top of the batter.
Bake for 45 to 55 minutes until the crust is golden brown and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool in pan for 10 minutes before turning out onto a wire rack.
tips: Different beer styles alter the profile: light lagers give a mild yeast flavor, while ambers and stouts give deep, rich malty undertones.

title: Pecan Toffee Christmas Crack
description: Holiday cracker toffee layered with toasted pecans, crisp caramelized brown sugar butter, and decadent melted chocolate.
author: Brandon Family
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a large rimmed cookie sheet with parchment paper.
Arrange crackers in a single tight layer across the baking sheet.
In a heavy saucepan, melt butter and dark brown sugar over medium heat. Bring to a rolling boil and cook without stirring for exactly 3 minutes.
Carefully pour hot toffee over crackers and spread gently with a spatula.
Bake in oven for 5 to 7 minutes until bubbling vigorously across the entire pan.
Remove and immediately scatter chocolate chips across the surface. Let sit for 2 minutes to melt, then spread into an even chocolate layer.
Top with chopped toasted pecans and a sprinkle of flaky sea salt.
Chill in refrigerator for 45 minutes until set, then break into shards.
tips: Store in an airtight container in the freezer for up to 3 weeks for an icy, crisp sweet treat.

title: Creamy Roasted Tomato Soup
description: Velvety roasted tomato soup infused with garlic, fresh basil, and a touch of heavy cream. Pairs impeccably with grilled cheese.
author: Brandon Family
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Arrange tomatoes, garlic cloves, and onion on a large baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast for 35 to 40 minutes until tomatoes are tender and slightly charred on edges.
Transfer roasted vegetables and juices into a Dutch oven.
Add vegetable broth and fresh basil leaves. Bring to a simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Use an immersion blender to puree the soup until completely smooth and velvety.
Stir in heavy cream and season with additional salt and freshly cracked pepper to taste.
Ladle hot into bowls and garnish with extra basil and a drizzle of olive oil.
tips: Roasting the tomatoes concentrates the natural sugars and creates an incomparably deeper flavor than canned tomatoes.
